data.summary: Microscopist on 4 field(s): density lower vs DMSO; 9 observations; candidates: Microtubule stabilizers

observations.finding: Treated green channel far brighter and more heterogeneous than DMSO control (which is blurry/dim diffuse green). Thick green cables/bundles in interphase cells and intensely bright yellow-green rounded mitotic cells with coarse bundled texture in all 4 fields.

Agrees with top deviations: tub_mean z +29.7 (0.697 vs 0.262 control), tub_std z +37.7 (0.567 vs 0.125) and tub_glcm_contrast z +115.0 (0.014 vs 0.002) - increased polymer mass and high texture contrast/bundling.

Blue nuclei more irregular, lobed and less round vs small oval nuclei in control (control out-of-focus but regular ovals still discernible). Lower right cluster in f_6bb7cf105224 and many cells in other fields show bi-lobed/multipolar/micronucleated figures and increased eccentricity.
Agrees with nuc_form_factor z -23.8 (0.825 vs 0.915), nuc_solidity z -21.7 (0.941 vs 0.972) and nuc_eccentricity z +9.1 (0.643 vs 0.600) - less circular, less solid, more elongated/irregular nuclei.
Overall DAPI intensity appears fainter/more diffuse in interphase nuclei; condensed figures are bright but population mean lower than control.
Red F-actin shows prominent cortical rings and ruffled edges around enlarged rounded cells, overall red brighter than dim diffuse red in DMSO control.
Matches act_mean z +6.1 (0.505 vs 0.274). Likely secondary to rounding/mitotic arrest, not diffuse actin loss.

Fields show markedly lower confluence with many rounded mitotic-arrest-like cells and aberrant spindles; DMSO is confluent monolayer. No cell-number feature provided to compare - not covered by measurements.

notable_cells.why: large flat cell with multiple green bundled cables converging to abnormal multipolar figure and lobed blue nucleus - example of stabilized microtubule bundles/ aberrant spindle
intense green ring/bundle around blue nucleus and neighboring bright yellow-green rounded mitotic cells with monopolar/bundled appearance - mitotic arrest pattern

candidate_mechanisms.why: Extreme increase in tubulin amount/variance/texture (z ~30-115) with formation of thick bundles/cables and accumulation of bright rounded mitotic cells and irregular lobed nuclei is classic stabilizer (taxol-like) phenotype; distinct from destabilizers which reduce polymer signal and from Aurora/Eg5 which do not produce massive tub_mean increase.

report.uncertainty: DMSO control composite f_b936a0c0d2e0 is severely out-of-focus/blurry, limiting precise nuclear/actin detail comparison, but brightness and bulk morphology differences remain clear. Grayscale channels not available - reading stains by colour only.

reflection.text:
This blinded run was scored as correct: we submitted Microtubule stabilizers p=0.96 and unblinding revealed docetaxel, PubChem CID 148124, ChEMBL CHEMBL3545252 with mechanisms Tubulin inhibitor / Tubulin stabiliser, name and BBBC021 structure agree (e11, e12). The hypothesis was already fixed before unblinding and the protocol NSC was unanimous, so the reflection is about why the image-based call was well supported and where ambiguity remained.

What the evidence got right: The discriminative acquisitions captured an extreme, dose-replicated tubulin phenotype. e2 at 0.1 uM: tub_glcm_contrast z=+115.0, tub_std +37.7, tub_mean +29.7 on 232 cells. e3 at 0.01 uM: tub_glcm_contrast +102.7, tub_mean +41.2, tub_std +36.4 on 91 cells. e6 at 0.03 uM: tub_glcm_contrast +62.9, tub_std +22.3, nuc_form_factor -26.2 on 280 cells. e7 at 1 uM: tub_glcm_contrast +108.2, tub_std +32.4, tub_mean +25.1 on 165 cells. Direction and magnitude were consistent from 0.01 to 1 uM, with high-contrast textural signal indicating thick bundles, not diffuse loss. e4 describe_phenotype independently reported density lower vs DMSO but microscopist on 4 fields saw thick bundles / mitotic-arrest-like cells with candidate Microtubule stabilizers, no destabilizer call. e5 (2 wells) and e8 (4 wells) compare_to_reference_atlas gave NSC vote Microtubule stabilizers 2/2 then 4/4, per-well 1-NN similarities 0.842-0.852 in the verdict, summed similarity 3.387. That unanimous 1-NN vote across four independent doses is what justified e9 update_hypotheses 0.96 / 0.02 / 0.01 / 0.01 and e10 submit_conclusion. The review critique approved for the same reason: the direction opposes Microtubule destabilizers, which would lower polymer signal, and Aurora/Eg5 inhibitors cannot explain a +22 to +41 SD increase in tub_mean/std/contrast.

What could have misled and why it did not change the call: e5/e8 also reported k-neighbour 5/10 stabilizers, 5/10 destabilizers, a tie that on its own looks ambiguous. The acquisition choice matters here: we sampled 4 doses spanning 0.01-1 uM via list_available_experiments e1 (0.0003-1 uM, 4 wells per condition available) specifically to test dose-dependency rather than relying on a single well. The NSC gap - mean similarity 0.846 for stabilizer matches vs 0.649 for next best, per review - and unanimous 1-NN across all doses resolved the k=10 tie. It is a nearest-reference atlas artifact, not a biological contradiction.

What was missed/limited: We did not acquire the lowest doses 0.0003-0.001 uM to define threshold or EC50, and we did not acquire an explicit DMSO well in this run, relying on z-scores against the plate reference and the microscopist's DMSO comparison in e4. Budget was exhausted after 4 wells (0 left), so no further affordable well could have flipped a 4-0 NSC. e13 PubMed 'docetaxel microtubule stabilizer mechanism' returned 104 hits and e14 'taxane microtubule bundling' returned 0 hits in this run, and none of the PMIDs returned in Literatures map directly to this BBBC021 bundling phenotype, so we correctly did not anchor the blinded call on literature but on replicated morphology and NSC distance. No orthogonal biochemistry (tubulin polymerization, EB1 comets, FACS) was performed blinded; that was appropriately proposed only as next_experiment_if_this_were_a_real_lab.

Calibration: p=0.96 with residual mass to destabilizers 0.02 reflects the remaining k-neighbour ambiguity and lack of lowest-dose/pharmacology data, while acknowledging that four independent doses with the same extreme bundling signature and unanimous NSC make a stabilizer misclassification very unlikely. No clinical inference is intended; this is a screening morphology call only.
